dedupe_keys.name: space weather prediction testbed 2026 bulk electric system exercise geomagnetic storm operator in the loop

description: The 2026 Bulk Electric System exercise of NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Testbed is a displaced-real-time, operator-in-the-loop simulation of an impactful geomagnetic storm affecting the bulk electric system in the United States and Canada, used to evaluate prototype SWPC decision-support services for preparedness, response, recovery and all-clear decisions. It was held in person at SWPC in Boulder, Colorado, in two identical 2.5-day sessions on 18 to 20 and 25 to 27 August 2026, for reliability coordinators, transmission operators and planners, balancing authorities, GMD programme leads and researchers. Its objectives were to test ensemble forecasts of storm onset with confidence intervals, probabilistic intensity forecasts, regional geoelectric hazard and risk guidance with the likelihood of exceeding user thresholds, unbounded intensity scaling such as the Hp index instead of Kp, and storm duration forecasts including sequential CME arrivals. The exercise page is accessible online as free HTML, with the testbed's major storm geoelectric simulations alongside. Caveats: the page describes the design and objectives; findings had not been published there on 26 September 2026, and testbed products are experimental. It illustrates emergency response exercising and digital decision support for space weather resilience of power grids; related records are the major storm geoelectric simulations and SWPC geoelectric field maps.
